title: Geometrically integral base refinement of a pointed finite-over-smooth diagram
statement: Let $S_0,Y_0$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $n\geq0$, and let $h_0:Y_0\to S_0$ be smooth of relative dimension $n$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and of finite presentation (locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated) [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\pi_0:W_0\to Y_0$ be a finite morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] of schemes and let $w_0\in W_0$, $y_0=\pi_0(w_0)$, $s_0=h_0(y_0)$ satisfy $\pi_0^{-1}(\{y_0\})=\{w_0\}$. Assume that $\kappa(y_0)/\kappa(s_0)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is a rational function field in finitely many algebraically independent variables. There exist an affine scheme $S_1$, a point $s_1\in S_1$, an etale morphism $e:S_1\to S_0$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] with $e(s_1)=s_0$ and $\kappa(s_0)\to\kappa(s_1)$ an isomorphism, and a quasi-compact open subscheme $V\subseteq Y_0\times_{S_0}S_1$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $v:V\to Y_0$ and $h_1:V\to S_1$ for the projections, $W_1=W_0\times_{Y_0}V$, $\rho:W_1\to W_0$ and $\pi_1:W_1\to V$. Then $h_1$ is smooth of relative dimension $n$ and every fibre of $h_1$ remains integral after every extension of its residue field [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme]. Both $v$ and $\rho$ are etale. There is exactly one $y_1\in V$ mapping to $(y_0,s_1)$, and exactly one $w_1\in W_1$ over $y_1$; these satisfy $\rho(w_1)=w_0$, $\pi_1^{-1}(\{y_1\})=\{w_1\}$, and $\pi_1$ is finite. The induced maps $\kappa(y_0)\to\kappa(y_1)$ and $\kappa(w_0)\to\kappa(w_1)$ are isomorphisms, compatible with the structural maps from $\kappa(s_0)$ and with $\kappa(s_0)\to\kappa(s_1)$. In particular $\kappa(y_1)/\kappa(s_1)$ is the same rational function extension under these identifications.

source.place: Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, proof from the connected component T through the outer pullback diagram and the marked residue-field identifications.

proof.text: Put k = κ(s₀), C = (Y₀)_{s₀}, and c = h₀.asFiber(y₀) [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. The Mathlib instance from LocallyOfFinitePresentation to LocallyOfFiniteType and finite-type base change [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change] give C finite type; smooth base change [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] makes C smooth. The fibre inclusion is a preimmersion and is surjective on stalks. A surjection of local rings induces a surjection on residue fields, which is also injective since it is a field map [def-weil-residue-field]. Thus its residue-field map is an isomorphism. Naturality of residue-field points [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality], applied also to h₀.asFiberHom(y₀), identifies this isomorphism with an isomorphism over k. Transport the finite rational-function-field presentation to κ(c). The images of the polynomial variables form an algebraically independent family, and every element is a quotient of evaluated polynomials; hence they generate κ(c) as a field [def-trf-purely-transcendental-extension]. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-component-pure-transcendental] to get an open connected component T containing c which is geometrically integral, hence geometrically irreducible [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-pc-integral-scheme].

source.place: Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, proof: connected component T, application of Tag 057J, and the outer pullback diagram.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-geometrically-integral-fibre-neighbourhood] to h₀, s₀ and T. It supplies S₁, e, s₁, the residue-field isomorphism α, and the quasi-compact open V with geometrically integral structure morphism h₁ and the specified equality of embedded open fibres. Smooth base change followed by the open inclusion, which is smooth of relative dimension zero in Mathlib, gives SmoothOfRelativeDimension n h₁ [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Open immersions are etale and etale maps compose [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]; etale base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] gives etale v and ρ. Finite base change gives finite π₁ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, proof: connected component T, application of Tag 057J, and the outer pullback diagram.

proof.text: Write q : Y₀ ×_{S₀} S₁ → S₁. The canonical fibre comparison F : q^{-1}(s₁) → (Y₀)_{e(s₁)} is the pullback of Spec(α) [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-fibre-product]. Mathlib isPullback_fiberToSpecResidueField_of_isPullback proves this square cartesian. Since Spec(α) is an isomorphism, F is an isomorphism. Compose with transport along e(s₁) = s₀ to obtain E onto C and take c₁ = E⁻¹(c). The equality of embedded open fibres from step 2 puts c₁ in the inverse image of V. Its image under the fibre inclusion gives y₁ in V with the required projections. For uniqueness, use [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points]: the tensor pushout of a field map along an isomorphism is isomorphic to the other field, so its spectrum has one point. The open inclusion is injective, so the same uniqueness holds in V.

source.place: Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, proof: connected component T, application of Tag 057J, and the outer pullback diagram.

proof.text: The residue-field map of the first projection at any point over s₁ is an isomorphism. To see this without tensor residue-field calculations, apply the fibre comparison of step 3 to that point. Both fibre inclusions are surjective on stalks, so their residue-field maps are isomorphisms by step 1; the fibre comparison is itself an isomorphism, hence so is its residue-field map. The commutative square of projections and residueFieldMap_comp cancel the source-fibre residue isomorphism and give the assertion. Compose with the open inclusion to get β : κ(y₀) ≅ κ(y₁). Functoriality of residue-field maps [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality], transported by residueFieldCongr, proves the first displayed structural square.

source.place: Tag 057K, lemma-local-local-structure-finite-type, proof: connected component T, application of Tag 057J, and the outer pullback diagram.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-points] to obtain w₁ over (w₀,y₁). For any point over y₁, commutativity of the pullback [def-pc-fibre-product] puts its first projection in π₀⁻¹({y₀}), so this projection is w₀. The fixed-pair uniqueness argument of step 3, now using β, proves that this point is w₁; this gives π₁⁻¹({y₁}) = {w₁}. The residue-field argument of step 4, now applied to π₀ and v, proves the isomorphism κ(w₀) → κ(w₁). Functoriality and point transport [lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-point-naturality] give the second square. Finally extend α coefficientwise to the polynomial rings and then to their fraction fields. Compose this fraction-field equivalence with the original rational presentation and β⁻¹. The first square proves that this composite is an algebra equivalence over κ(s₁), with the same finite set of variables.
